method: Targeted local profiles using Scalene's legacy tracer and CPU-only mode after the default memory profiler proved disproportionately expensive.

profiles.command: uv run scalene run --use-legacy-tracer --cpu-only --profile-only voiage -o <temporary-json> profile_scalene.py

attribution.interpretation: Import-time jsonschema loading, with most samples recorded as system time.
Import-time schema construction and validation dependencies.

profiles.command: uv run scalene run --use-legacy-tracer --cpu-only --profile-only repo_harness -o <temporary-json> scripts/repo_harness.py

attribution.interpretation: Filesystem traversal and file reads dominate; profiler overhead increases the absolute wall time.
The 1,000-replicate Python loop repeatedly allocates bootstrap samples and calls EVPI/EVPPI; it is the dominant measured hotspot.
Plot rendering is not the primary cost.

complementary_evidence.result: The full serial run identified paper bootstrap, repository traversal, wheel/subprocess setup, and Yggdrasil subprocess reconciliation as the four largest tests.
An isolated voiage.schema import took about 25.5 seconds, including about 16.9 seconds constructing rfc3987_syntax parsers reached through eager jsonschema imports.
Serial pytest used 290.7 user seconds over 3369.2 wall seconds, demonstrating that CPU profiling alone cannot explain subprocess, import, and filesystem latency.

tool_limitations: The default Scalene memory profile was stopped after 340 seconds when it reached roughly 4 GB resident memory and repeatedly attempted unavailable TensorFlow profiling hooks; it materially distorted the small workload.
A pytest-target profile did not collect application samples because the executable lived under .venv/bin; profiling the underlying repository script directly produced usable evidence.

Scalene does not aggregate the work of the many fresh child interpreters used by subprocess-contract tests into a useful parent profile; pytest durations, importtime, and process observations are required alongside it.
Percentages describe sampled time within each profile and must not be compared as absolute timings across different commands.

required_experiments.change: Lazy-load jsonschema-backed validators and schema-only contracts.
required_experiments.gate: Top-level import below five seconds with stable symbols and unchanged validation errors.

required_experiments.change: Scan Git-tracked text paths rather than recursive checkout contents.
required_experiments.gate: Identical injected-marker detection and a warm wall-time reduction of at least 80%.

required_experiments.change: Batch or vectorize resampling and reuse immutable ParameterSet/net-benefit structures where numerically equivalent.
required_experiments.gate: Byte-identical tracked tables, fixed-seed intervals within the declared tolerance, and a measured speedup.

required_experiments.change: Consolidate independent probes per clean interpreter and reuse built wheels/artifacts.
required_experiments.gate: Preserve clean-process isolation, failure attribution, and installed-artifact semantics.

required_experiments.change: Repair order-dependent lazy-module state and benchmark bounded 4, 6, and 8 worker work-stealing lanes with serial groups.
required_experiments.gate: Same pass/fail set as serial, deterministic seeds, retained coverage, and lower peak memory than the eight-worker baseline.
